findings.text: follow-on: `assert not in_flight.get("folded_findings"), in_flight` is inert. The in-flight report is returned from a different branch of dispatch_repair_for_run (reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:1150, the resumed path) which carries no folded_findings key at all, so `.get(...)` is None and the assertion holds whatever the code does — including a regression that folds the round's findings while the round is still in flight, which is the exact behaviour the docstring at recover_repair_dispatch.py:512-529 says must not happen. The earlier iteration of this assertion (`== []`, logs/followon.log) failed on the absent key rather than on a fold, and it was widened to the `.get` form instead of the in-flight branch being made to report `folded_findings: []`; the in-flight half of the guard therefore reddens under no code change.

follow-on: the after_suite evidence log carries no header and no terminating status line — its first line is pytest progress dots, not the revision/tree/command header the manifest contract requires for a scratch-tree measurement, and it ends at `182 passed in 584.24s` with no bare `EXIT=<code>` line. The suite result therefore cannot be tied to a revision or re-run from the log's own content, and the gate's exit status is unread there (it survives only in after_suite.exit_status in the manifest); after_suite.command is likewise a prose description of the target set rather than the literal command, so the record cannot be replayed. The gate log the same node kept for the head arm (logs/gate-head.log) does carry both, so the omission is specific to the follow-on run.

item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete at 1de59a176, five commits (37abd242, 492418fb, a2ab0640, 28efb60c, 1de59a176), baseline_suite (negative-control.log, 1 failure, EXIT=1), after_suite (gate-followon.log, 0 failures, EXIT=0) and two negative-control logs, one per half of the change.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared fence is the six files named in the prompt (recovery_review_dispatch.py, recovery_repair_dispatch.py, review_dispositions.py, obligations.py, the test module, the landing fragment); the 492418fb..1de59a176 diff touches exactly those six and nothing else.

justifications.durability: the strong guards are independent of the value under test — tests/test_a_review_waits_for_its_repair.py:374 reads the written record back through repair.blocking_finding_dispositions and asserts the disposition is 'folded' (it would read 'open' if the fold regressed), :376 asserts the disposition names the round node, and :385-386 assert the re-review dispatches — but the in-flight assertion at :358 is inert (see the finding), and the negative control for the fold manifests as a KeyError at :368 rather than a behavioural assertion, so one half of the guard is unprotected.
justifications.evidence: the gate ran and its result is recorded — the manifest's after_suite names gate-followon.log at 182 passed with exit_status 0, and its baseline_suite names negative-control.log at 1 failure with exit_status 1 — but gate-followon.log carries no revision header and no EXIT= line and its command field is prose, so the pass cannot be re-run or tied to a revision by the record alone; I re-ran the named test file at 1de59a176 myself (4 passed, EXIT=0) rather than rest on the unreadable log.
justifications.fit: the added names are mechanism-descriptive (reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:459 _fold_findings_into_round, :512 _fold_a_landed_round, reckon/crew/review_dispositions.py:489 dispose_commands) with no plan, ticket or stage identifier, and the module's local-import and report-dict idiom is followed.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:512 folds each open blocking finding into the round through review_dispositions.record_finding_disposition at the round's node id, so the repaired head's re-review is not refused; the plan words the fold at composition and the landed change takes it at landing (recovery_repair_dispatch.py:752-757), a documented deviation whose required outcome — 'the repaired head's re-review is therefore not refused' — the code and the new test both reach.
justifications.reuse: the change removes a duplication rather than adding one: obligations.py:1210 and recovery_review_dispatch.py:2099 now both call review_dispositions.dispose_commands, the single rendering beside the writer that stores the disposition, extending the owner the earlier review flagged; the fold reuses repair.blocking_finding_dispositions and review_dispositions.record_finding_disposition rather than deriving a second answer to either.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the 492418fb..1de59a176 diff (recovery_review_dispatch.py, recovery_repair_dispatch.py, review_dispositions.py, obligations.py, tests/test_a_review_waits_for_its_repair.py, the landing fragment) is inside the six declared write paths, and the change carries nothing the goal does not imply.
